questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before you carry a passenger in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle feels and handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show road rules like speed limits. They are white with black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars seem:
questions.explanation: Curved convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can limit the view of the motorcycle operator.
Allow the motorcycle operator to see as far to the sides as necessary.
Do not have to be worn if the motorcycle operator thinks their view would be limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle operator to see as far to the sides as necessary.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not dangerously limit your side vision. Any approved helmet lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Before mounting the motorcycle, your pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a full pre-ride inspection each time.

questions.question: To help provide space for drivers attempting to merge into your lane from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
Not worry about it, since they are the ones trying to merge.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Move to another lane if you can. This gives them safe space to merge.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while you are riding:

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes the steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, leave the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping will be easier than when riding without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
Stopping is about as easy as it is when riding without the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than when riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. This means you need more braking force to stop. Slowing and stopping take longer when going downhill and when carrying extra weight.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat. Only do this if you are sure which tire is flat.

questions.question: What formation keeps a group of riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space around them. Single-file is better for curves, turns, and entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, which is NOT a hazard?

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors, wind blasts, and objects passengers might throw. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you out of blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from entering your lane.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: On a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger ride?

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing, keep your headlight on all the time, and change your lane position when needed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes wobbling worse. Instead, hold the handlebars tight, slow down gradually by releasing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Avoid braking, as it can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Judge distances more easily than during the day.
Know that high beam headlights always make it hard to see.

questions.explanation: At night, ride slower and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use your high beam headlight when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Coming to a complete stop before you expect to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Over-braking causes you to lose traction and can lead to a crash.

questions.question: What may help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: Tightening the chain may fix slippage. If it does not work, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to pass the hazard.
Move to the shoulder instead of riding over the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight across at a steady speed. Trying to zigzag to fix the weaving is more dangerous than just riding straight.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check everything except the:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake for non-emergency stops.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The body removes about one drink per hour. Someone had eight drinks four hours ago. How many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do everything except:

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight unless you are following or meeting another vehicle.
